definitions.explanation: The Japanese syllabary writing systems, including hiragana and katakana. Contrasts with kanji (Chinese characters).

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}はまず{仮名|かな}を{習|なら}う。
{仮名|かな}で{書|か}いてください。
{平仮名|ひらがな}と{片仮名|かたかな}を{合|あ}わせて{仮名|かな}と{言|い}う。
examples.english: Hiragana and katakana together are called kana.

notes:
WRITING: Can also be written as かな in hiragana.

TYPES:
・{平仮名|ひらがな} (hiragana) - cursive syllabary
・{片仮名|かたかな} (katakana) - angular syllabary

ETYMOLOGY: {仮|か} means 'temporary/borrowed' and {名|な} means 'name/character'. Kana were originally simplified forms of kanji used for their phonetic value.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{仮名|かな}{遣|づか}い (kana orthography)
・{仮名|かな}{書|が}き (writing in kana)
